grades.quote: Exceptions and interrupts will interrupt the currently executing program and switch the control flow to the entry of the exception/interrupt handler to start execution.
grades.reason: General LoongArch overview of exceptions and interrupts and the types of exception. It says control flow switches to the handler entry, but it does not say how the entry address is chosen.

grades.quote: If the hart encounters an exception while executing in M-mode with the `mnstatus` .NMIE bit clear, the actions taken are the same as if the exception had occurred while `mnstatus` .NMIE were set, except that the program counter is set to the RNMI exception trap handler address.
grades.reason: RISC-V Smrnmi passage. It shows the handler address depends on the trap type (RNMI interrupt or an exception) and on the mnstatus.NMIE state. It covers only the RNMI case, not general trap vectoring.

grades.quote: This register is used to configure the entry base address for general exceptions and interrupts.
grades.reason: The LoongArch EENTRY register holds the entry base address for general exceptions and interrupts, so it is a central configuration element. The passage does not describe per-exception offsets or the separate TLB refill entry.
These CRMD fields (IE, DA, PG) cover interrupt enable and address translation mode on exception entry and return. They say nothing about how the handler entry address is selected.
